newsitem.title: UK: Brent crude firmer, wet cargo may have traded.
newsitem.headline: Brent crude firmer, wet cargo may have traded.

text.p: A cargo of physical Brent crude was heard to have traded on Wednesday but details were not yet available, traders said.
The cargo (due to load Feb 5-7) had been offered earlier at a strong Feb Brent +2 cents and traders close to the market felt a level near this may have been achieved.
"There is a bit of strength in the prompt market. A bit of hype for the moment, but overall it looks black. Margins are poor and buyers are covered," one said.
March IPE Brent gained ground over the morning to trade at 1241 GMT up 32 cents at $22.68 a barrel.
Only one Brent cargo was due to turn wet on Wednesday. This was offered at Feb Brent +2 cents by one of the companies in the chain on Wednesday but was heard to have been since passed on.
On Thursday there are two cargoes scheduled to turn wet with only three seen in the original schedule for Friday.
The revised January Ekofisk programme was due to be released on Wednesday but equity holders said they did not expect the February loading programme until Friday.
Cargoes currently loading were running around four days behind schedule, one lifter said.
Mar/Apr traded twice at +43 cents and Feb/Mar leaping ahead to move at +38 cents.
CFD action was light as sellers moved off. Most were reluctant to show firm offers, brokers said.
A Feb 24-28 traded at April Brent +29 cents.

North Sea crude availabilities for February saw good Oseberg supplies, two Statfjord cargoes loading around the 10th of the month and then none until the third decade, two Gullfaks C to the end of the month, no remaining Draugen cargoes and a Troll with month end option.
Urals talk was light with levels holding stable.
